method.label: Cancel factorials and complete the square

annotationRationale: Simplifying consecutive factorials produces a quadratic, which is solved by completing the square.
sourceMethod: Follows the official solution: divide by n!, expand, complete the square, and use positivity to select n=19.

review.mathCheck: Since n! is nonzero, cancellation gives n²+4n+3=440 and hence (n+2)²=441. The roots are 19 and −23; positivity selects 19, whose digit sum is 10, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently phrased adaptation of official solution 6 on page 3: cancel factorials, complete the square, and select the positive root. The added factorial expansions make the method reconstructible.
review.annotationCheck: Both factorial cancellation and completing the square are central assessed skills; no additional integer-equation or factoring node is needed.
